sourceTexts.Matthew 6:7-8: But when ye pray, use not vain repetitions, as the heathen do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking. Be not ye therefore like unto them: for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him.
sourceTexts.Micah 7:18-19: Who is a God like unto thee, that pardoneth iniquity, and passeth by the transgression of the remnant of his heritage? he retaineth not his anger for ever, because he delighteth in mercy. He will turn again, he will have compassion upon us; he will subdue our iniquities; and thou wilt cast all their sins into the depths of the sea.
sourceTexts.Numbers 6:24-26: The Lord bless thee, and keep thee: The LORD make his face shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee: The LORD lift up his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace.
sourceTexts.Philippians 3:13-14: Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before, I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.
sourceTexts.Philippians 3:7-8: But what things were gain to me, those I counted loss for Christ.
sourceTexts.Philippians 4:11-13: Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content. I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound: every where and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need. I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
sourceTexts.Philippians 4:6-7: Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
sourceTexts.Proverbs 22:24-25: Make no friendship with an angry man; and with a furious man shalt thou not go: Lest thou learn his ways, and get a snare to thy soul.
sourceTexts.Proverbs 3:5-6: Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.
sourceTexts.Proverbs 3:9-10: Honour the LORD with thy substance, and with the firstfruits of all thine increase: So shall thy barns be filled with plenty, and thy presses shall burst out with new wine.
sourceTexts.Psalm 100:1: Make a joyful noise unto the Lord, all ye lands.
sourceTexts.Psalm 100:1-2: Make a joyful noise unto the LORD, all ye lands. Serve the LORD with gladness: come before his presence with singing.
sourceTexts.Psalm 100:1-5: Make a joyful noise unto the LORD, all ye lands. Serve the LORD with gladness: come before his presence with singing. Know ye that the LORD he is God: it is he that hath made us, and not we ourselves; we are his people, and the sheep of his pasture. Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him, and bless his name. For the LORD is good; his mercy is everlasting; and his truth endureth to all generations.
sourceTexts.Psalm 100:2: Serve the Lord with gladness: come before his presence with singing.
sourceTexts.Psalm 100:3: Know ye that the Lord he is God: it is he that hath made us, and not we ourselves.
sourceTexts.Psalm 100:4: Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him, and bless his name.
sourceTexts.Psalm 100:5: The Lord is good; his mercy is everlasting.
sourceTexts.Psalm 102:17: He will regard the prayer of the destitute, and not despise their prayer.
sourceTexts.Psalm 103:1: Bless the Lord, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name.
sourceTexts.Psalm 103:1-2: Bless the LORD, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name. Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits:
sourceTexts.Psalm 103:1-5: Bless the LORD, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name. Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits: Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases; Who redeemeth thy life from destruction; who crowneth thee with lovingkindness and tender mercies; Who satisfieth thy mouth with good things; so that thy youth is renewed like the eagle's.
sourceTexts.Psalm 103:11: For as the heaven is high above the earth, so great is his mercy toward them that fear him.
sourceTexts.Psalm 103:12: As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us.
sourceTexts.Psalm 103:13: Like as a father pitieth his children, so the Lord pitieth them that fear him.
sourceTexts.Psalm 103:13-14: Like as a father pitieth his children, so the LORD pitieth them that fear him. For he knoweth our frame; he remembereth that we are dust.
sourceTexts.Psalm 103:17: But the mercy of the Lord is from everlasting to everlasting upon them that fear him.
sourceTexts.Psalm 103:2: Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits.
sourceTexts.Psalm 103:2-3: Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits: Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases.
sourceTexts.Psalm 103:3: Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases;
sourceTexts.Psalm 103:4: Who redeemeth thy life from destruction; who crowneth thee with lovingkindness.
sourceTexts.Psalm 103:5: Who satisfieth thy mouth with good things; so that thy youth is renewed like the eagle's.
sourceTexts.Psalm 103:8: The Lord is merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and plenteous in mercy.
sourceTexts.Psalm 104:1: Bless the Lord, O my soul. O Lord my God, thou art very great.
sourceTexts.Psalm 104:24: O LORD, how manifold are thy works! in wisdom hast thou made them all: the earth is full of thy riches.
sourceTexts.Psalm 104:33: I will sing unto the Lord as long as I live: I will sing praise to my God while I have my being.
sourceTexts.Psalm 105:1: O give thanks unto the Lord; call upon his name: make known his deeds among the people.
sourceTexts.Psalm 105:17: He sent a man before them, even Joseph, who was sold for a servant:
sourceTexts.Psalm 106:1: Praise ye the Lord. O give thanks unto the Lord; for he is good.
sourceTexts.Psalm 107:1: O give thanks unto the LORD, for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.
sourceTexts.Psalm 107:14: He brought them out of darkness and the shadow of death, and brake their bands in sunder.
sourceTexts.Psalm 107:8: Oh that men would praise the Lord for his goodness, and for his wonderful works to the children of men!
sourceTexts.Psalm 107:9: For he satisfieth the longing soul, and filleth the hungry soul with goodness.
sourceTexts.Psalm 108:1: O God, my heart is fixed; I will sing and give praise, even with my glory.
sourceTexts.Psalm 108:4: For thy mercy is great above the heavens: and thy truth reacheth unto the clouds.
sourceTexts.Psalm 109:30: I will greatly praise the Lord with my mouth; yea, I will praise him among the multitude.
sourceTexts.Psalm 10:14: Thou hast seen it; for thou beholdest mischief and spite, to requite it with thy hand: the poor committeth himself unto thee; thou art the helper of the fatherless.
sourceTexts.Psalm 10:17: LORD, thou hast heard the desire of the humble: thou wilt prepare their heart, thou wilt cause thine ear to hear:
sourceTexts.Psalm 111:1: Praise ye the Lord. I will praise the Lord with my whole heart.
sourceTexts.Psalm 111:4: He hath made his wonderful works to be remembered: the Lord is gracious and full of compassion.
sourceTexts.Psalm 112:1: Praise ye the Lord. Blessed is the man that feareth the Lord.
sourceTexts.Psalm 112:4: Unto the upright there ariseth light in the darkness: he is gracious, and full of compassion, and righteous.
sourceTexts.Psalm 113:2: Blessed be the name of the Lord from this time forth and for evermore.
sourceTexts.Psalm 113:3: From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same the LORD's name is to be praised.
sourceTexts.Psalm 113:9: He maketh the barren woman to keep house, and to be a joyful mother of children. Praise ye the LORD.
sourceTexts.Psalm 115:12: The Lord hath been mindful of us: he will bless us.
sourceTexts.Psalm 116:1: I love the Lord, because he hath heard my voice and my supplications.
sourceTexts.Psalm 116:1-2: I love the Lord, because he hath heard my voice and my supplications. Because he hath inclined his ear unto me, therefore will I call upon him as long as I live.
sourceTexts.Psalm 116:17: I will offer to thee the sacrifice of thanksgiving, and will call upon the name of the LORD.
sourceTexts.Psalm 116:2: Because he hath inclined his ear unto me, therefore will I call upon him as long as I live.
sourceTexts.Psalm 116:5: Gracious is the Lord, and righteous; yea, our God is merciful.
sourceTexts.Psalm 116:7: Return unto thy rest, O my soul; for the LORD hath dealt bountifully with thee.
sourceTexts.Psalm 117:1: O praise the Lord, all ye nations: praise him, all ye people.
sourceTexts.Psalm 117:2: For his merciful kindness is great toward us: and the truth of the Lord endureth for ever.
sourceTexts.Psalm 118:1: O give thanks unto the Lord; for he is good: because his mercy endureth for ever.
sourceTexts.Psalm 118:14: The Lord is my strength and song.
sourceTexts.Psalm 118:17: I shall not die, but live, and declare the works of the Lord.
sourceTexts.Psalm 118:21: I will praise thee: for thou hast heard me, and art become my salvation.
sourceTexts.Psalm 118:23: This is the Lord's doing; it is marvellous in our eyes.
sourceTexts.Psalm 118:24: This is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.
sourceTexts.Psalm 118:28: Thou art my God, and I will praise thee: thou art my God, I will exalt thee.
sourceTexts.Psalm 118:29: O give thanks unto the Lord; for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.
sourceTexts.Psalm 118:5: I called upon the Lord in distress: the Lord answered me, and set me in a large place.
sourceTexts.Psalm 118:6: The Lord is on my side; I will not fear.
sourceTexts.Psalm 118:8: It is better to trust in the Lord than to put confidence in man.
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:103: How sweet are thy words unto my taste! yea, sweeter than honey to my mouth!
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:105: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:11: Thy word have I hid in mine heart, that I might not sin against thee.
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:111: Thy testimonies have I taken as an heritage for ever: for they are the rejoicing of my heart.
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:114: Thou art my hiding place and my shield: I hope in thy word.
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:116: Uphold me according unto thy word, that I may live: and let me not be ashamed of my hope.
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:130: The entrance of thy words giveth light; it giveth understanding unto the simple.
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:140: Thy word is very pure: therefore thy servant loveth it.
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:147: I prevented the dawning of the morning, and cried: I hoped in thy word.
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:151: Thou art near, O Lord; and all thy commandments are truth.
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:160: Thy word is true from the beginning: and every one of thy righteous judgments endureth for ever.
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:162: I rejoice at thy word, as one that findeth great spoil.
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:165: Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:174: I have longed for thy salvation, O Lord; and thy law is my delight.
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:175: Let my soul live, and it shall praise thee; and let thy judgments help me.
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:18: Open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of thy law.
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:24: Thy testimonies also are my delight and my counsellors.
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:27: Make me to understand the way of thy precepts: so shall I talk of thy wondrous works.
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:28: My soul melteth for heaviness: strengthen thou me according unto thy word.
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:32: I will run the way of thy commandments, when thou shalt enlarge my heart.
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:45: And I will walk at liberty: for I seek thy precepts.
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:50: This is my comfort in my affliction: for thy word hath quickened me.
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:65: Thou hast dealt well with thy servant, O Lord, according unto thy word.
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:68: Thou art good, and doest good; teach me thy statutes.
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:73: Thy hands have made me and fashioned me: give me understanding, that I may learn thy commandments.
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:76: Let, I pray thee, thy merciful kindness be for my comfort, according to thy word unto thy servant.
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:89: For ever, O LORD, thy word is settled in heaven.
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:9: Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word.
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:92: Unless thy law had been my delights, I should then have perished in mine affliction.
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:93: I will never forget thy precepts: for with them thou hast quickened me.
sourceTexts.Psalm 119:97: O how love I thy law! it is my meditation all the day.
sourceTexts.Psalm 120:7: I am for peace: but when I speak, they are for war.
sourceTexts.Psalm 121:1: I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help.
sourceTexts.Psalm 121:1-2: I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help. My help cometh from the Lord, which made heaven and earth.
sourceTexts.Psalm 121:2: My help cometh from the LORD, which made heaven and earth.
sourceTexts.Psalm 121:3: He will not suffer thy foot to be moved.
sourceTexts.Psalm 121:3-4: He will not suffer thy foot to be moved: he that keepeth thee will not slumber. Behold, he that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep.
sourceTexts.Psalm 121:4: Behold, he that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep.
sourceTexts.Psalm 121:5: The Lord is thy keeper: the Lord is thy shade upon thy right hand.
sourceTexts.Psalm 121:6: The sun shall not smite thee by day, nor the moon by night.
sourceTexts.Psalm 121:7: The Lord shall preserve thee from all evil: he shall preserve thy soul.
sourceTexts.Psalm 121:7-8: The LORD shall preserve thee from all evil: he shall preserve thy soul. The LORD shall preserve thy going out and thy coming in from this time forth, and even for evermore.
sourceTexts.Psalm 121:8: The Lord shall preserve thy going out and thy coming in.
sourceTexts.Psalm 122:7: Peace be within thy walls, and prosperity within thy palaces.
sourceTexts.Psalm 123:2: Behold, as the eyes of servants look unto the hand of their masters, and as the eyes of a maiden unto the hand of her mistress; so our eyes wait upon the LORD our God, until that he have mercy upon us.
sourceTexts.Psalm 124:8: Our help is in the name of the Lord, who made heaven and earth.
sourceTexts.Psalm 125:1: They that trust in the Lord shall be as mount Zion, which cannot be removed.
sourceTexts.Psalm 126:2: Then was our mouth filled with laughter, and our tongue with singing.
sourceTexts.Psalm 126:3: He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength.
sourceTexts.Psalm 126:5: They that sow in tears shall reap in joy.
sourceTexts.Psalm 126:5-6: They that sow in tears shall reap in joy. He that goeth forth and weepeth, bearing precious seed, shall doubtless come again with rejoicing, bringing his sheaves with him.
sourceTexts.Psalm 127:1: Except the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it: except the Lord keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain.
sourceTexts.Psalm 127:2: It is vain for you to rise up early, to sit up late, to eat the bread of sorrows: for so he giveth his beloved sleep.
sourceTexts.Psalm 127:3: Lo, children are an heritage of the LORD: and the fruit of the womb is his reward.
sourceTexts.Psalm 127:4: As arrows are in the hand of a mighty man; so are children of the youth.
sourceTexts.Psalm 128:1: Blessed is every one that feareth the Lord; that walketh in his ways.
sourceTexts.Psalm 128:3: Thy wife shall be as a fruitful vine by the sides of thine house: thy children like olive plants round about thy table.
sourceTexts.Psalm 12:6: The words of the Lord are pure words.
sourceTexts.Psalm 130:3: If thou, LORD, shouldest mark iniquities, O Lord, who shall stand?
sourceTexts.Psalm 130:4: But there is forgiveness with thee, that thou mayest be feared.
sourceTexts.Psalm 130:5: I wait for the LORD, my soul doth wait, and in his word do I hope.
sourceTexts.Psalm 130:5-6: I wait for the LORD, my soul doth wait, and in his word do I hope. My soul waiteth for the Lord more than they that watch for the morning: I say, more than they that watch for the morning.
sourceTexts.Psalm 130:7: Let Israel hope in the Lord: for with the Lord there is mercy.
sourceTexts.Psalm 131:1-2: Lord, my heart is not haughty, nor mine eyes lofty: neither do I exercise myself in great matters, or in things too high for me. Surely I have behaved and quieted myself, as a child that is weaned of his mother: my soul is even as a weaned child.
sourceTexts.Psalm 131:2: Surely I have behaved and quieted myself, as a child that is weaned of his mother: my soul is even as a weaned child.
sourceTexts.Psalm 131:3: Let Israel hope in the Lord from henceforth and for ever.
sourceTexts.Psalm 133:1: Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!
sourceTexts.Psalm 134:2: Lift up your hands in the sanctuary, and bless the Lord.
sourceTexts.Psalm 135:3: Praise the Lord; for the Lord is good: sing praises unto his name; for it is pleasant.
sourceTexts.Psalm 136:1: O give thanks unto the LORD; for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.
sourceTexts.Psalm 136:4: To him which alone doeth great wonders: for his mercy endureth for ever.
sourceTexts.Psalm 138:1: I will praise thee with my whole heart: before the gods will I sing praise unto thee.
sourceTexts.Psalm 138:3: In the day when I cried thou answeredst me, and strengthenedst me with strength in my soul.
sourceTexts.Psalm 138:7: Though I walk in the midst of trouble, thou wilt revive me: thou shalt stretch forth thine hand against the wrath of mine enemies.
sourceTexts.Psalm 138:8: The Lord will perfect that which concerneth me: thy mercy, O Lord, endureth for ever: forsake not the works of thine own hands.
sourceTexts.Psalm 139:1: O LORD, thou hast searched me, and known me.
sourceTexts.Psalm 139:12: Yea, the darkness hideth not from thee; but the night shineth as the day: the darkness and the light are both alike to thee.
sourceTexts.Psalm 139:13: For thou hast possessed my reins: thou hast covered me in my mother’s womb.
sourceTexts.Psalm 139:14: I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made: marvellous are thy works; and that my soul knoweth right well.
sourceTexts.Psalm 139:16: Thine eyes did see my substance, yet being unperfect; and in thy book all my members were written, which in continuance were fashioned, when as yet there was none of them.
sourceTexts.Psalm 139:17: How precious also are thy thoughts unto me, O God! how great is the sum of them!
sourceTexts.Psalm 139:23-24: Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts: And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.
sourceTexts.Psalm 139:3: Thou compassest my path and my lying down, and art acquainted with all my ways.
sourceTexts.Psalm 139:8: If I ascend up into heaven, thou art there: if I make my bed in hell, behold, thou art there.
sourceTexts.Psalm 13:1: How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD? for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me?
sourceTexts.Psalm 13:5: I have trusted in thy mercy; my heart shall rejoice in thy salvation.
sourceTexts.Psalm 142:3: When my spirit was overwhelmed within me, then thou knewest my path. In the way wherein I walked have they privily laid a snare for me.
sourceTexts.Psalm 142:7: Bring my soul out of prison, that I may praise thy name: the righteous shall compass me about; for thou shalt deal bountifully with me.
sourceTexts.Psalm 143:8: Cause me to hear thy lovingkindness in the morning; for in thee do I trust: cause me to know the way wherein I should walk.
sourceTexts.Psalm 144:1: Blessed be the LORD my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight.
sourceTexts.Psalm 145:1-3: I will extol thee, my God, O king; and I will bless thy name for ever and ever. Every day will I bless thee; and I will praise thy name for ever and ever. Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised; and his greatness is unsearchable.
sourceTexts.Psalm 145:14: The Lord upholdeth all that fall, and raiseth up all those that be bowed down.
sourceTexts.Psalm 145:16: Thou openest thine hand, and satisfiest the desire of every living thing.
sourceTexts.Psalm 145:18: The Lord is nigh unto all them that call upon him, to all that call upon him in truth.
sourceTexts.Psalm 145:2: Every day will I bless thee; and I will praise thy name for ever and ever.
sourceTexts.Psalm 145:8: The LORD is gracious, and full of compassion; slow to anger, and of great mercy.
sourceTexts.Psalm 145:9: The Lord is good to all: and his tender mercies are over all his works.
sourceTexts.Psalm 147:3: He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds.
sourceTexts.Psalm 147:7: Sing unto the LORD with thanksgiving; sing praise upon the harp unto our God:
sourceTexts.Psalm 148:13: Let them praise the name of the LORD: for his name alone is excellent.
sourceTexts.Psalm 14:5: God is in the generation of the righteous.
sourceTexts.Psalm 150:1-6: Praise ye the LORD. Praise God in his sanctuary: praise him in the firmament of his power. Praise him for his mighty acts: praise him according to his excellent greatness. Praise him with the sound of the trumpet: praise him with psaltery and harp. Praise him with timbrel and dance: praise him with stringed instruments and organs. Praise him upon the loud cymbals: praise him upon the high sounding cymbals. Let every thing that hath breath praise the LORD. Praise ye the LORD.
sourceTexts.Psalm 150:6: Let every thing that hath breath praise the LORD. Praise ye the LORD.
sourceTexts.Psalm 16:11: Thou wilt shew me the path of life: in thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore.
sourceTexts.Psalm 16:5: The LORD is the portion of mine inheritance and of my cup: thou maintainest my lot.
sourceTexts.Psalm 16:8: I have set the Lord always before me: because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved.
sourceTexts.Psalm 17:6: I have called upon thee, for thou wilt hear me, O God: incline thine ear unto me, and hear my speech.
sourceTexts.Psalm 18:2: The Lord is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer; my God, my strength, in whom I will trust.
sourceTexts.Psalm 18:32-33: It is God that girdeth me with strength, and maketh my way perfect. He maketh my feet like hinds' feet, and setteth me upon my high places.
sourceTexts.Psalm 19:14: Let the words of my mouth, and the meditation of my heart, be acceptable in thy sight, O Lord, my strength, and my redeemer.
sourceTexts.Psalm 19:7: The law of the LORD is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple.
sourceTexts.Psalm 1:1-3: Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful. But his delight is in the law of the LORD; and in his law doth he meditate day and night. And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.
sourceTexts.Psalm 20:4: Grant thee according to thine own heart, and fulfil all thy counsel.
sourceTexts.Psalm 22:1: My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? why art thou so far from helping me, and from the words of my roaring?
sourceTexts.Psalm 22:2: O my God, I cry in the day time, but thou hearest not; and in the night season, and am not silent.
sourceTexts.Psalm 22:4: Our fathers trusted in thee: they trusted, and thou didst deliver them.
sourceTexts.Psalm 22:9: But thou art he that took me out of the womb: thou didst make me hope when I was upon my mother’s breasts.
sourceTexts.Psalm 23:1: Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.
sourceTexts.Psalm 23:1-2: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want. He maketh me to lie down in green pastures.
sourceTexts.Psalm 23:1-4: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want. He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters. He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name's sake. Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.
sourceTexts.Psalm 23:2: He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters.
sourceTexts.Psalm 23:3: He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.
sourceTexts.Psalm 23:4: Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.
sourceTexts.Psalm 23:6: Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life: and I will dwell in the house of the LORD for ever.
sourceTexts.Psalm 25:16: Turn thee unto me, and have mercy upon me; for I am desolate and afflicted.
sourceTexts.Psalm 25:16-17: Turn thee unto me, and have mercy upon me; for I am desolate and afflicted. The troubles of my heart are enlarged: O bring thou me out of my distresses.
sourceTexts.Psalm 25:18: Look upon mine affliction and my pain; and forgive all my sins.
sourceTexts.Psalm 25:4: Shew me thy ways, O Lord; teach me thy paths.
sourceTexts.Psalm 25:4-5: Shew me thy ways, O Lord; teach me thy paths. Lead me in thy truth, and teach me: for thou art the God of my salvation.
sourceTexts.Psalm 25:5: Lead me in thy truth, and teach me: for thou art the God of my salvation.
sourceTexts.Psalm 25:9: The meek will he guide in judgment: and the meek will he teach his way.
sourceTexts.Psalm 26:1: I have trusted also in the Lord; therefore I shall not slide.
sourceTexts.Psalm 27:1: The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the Lord is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
sourceTexts.Psalm 27:10: When my father and my mother forsake me, then the LORD will take me up.
sourceTexts.Psalm 27:13: I had fainted, unless I had believed to see the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living.
sourceTexts.Psalm 27:13-14: I had fainted, unless I had believed to see the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living. Wait on the LORD: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart: wait, I say, on the LORD.
sourceTexts.Psalm 27:14: Wait on the LORD: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart: wait, I say, on the LORD.
sourceTexts.Psalm 27:4: One thing have I desired of the Lord, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life.
sourceTexts.Psalm 27:8: When thou saidst, Seek ye my face; my heart said unto thee, Thy face, LORD, will I seek.
sourceTexts.Psalm 28:7: The Lord is my strength and my shield; my heart trusted in him, and I am helped: therefore my heart greatly rejoiceth.
sourceTexts.Psalm 29:11: The Lord will give strength unto his people; the Lord will bless his people with peace.
sourceTexts.Psalm 30:4: Sing unto the LORD, O ye saints of his, and give thanks at the remembrance of his holiness.
sourceTexts.Psalm 30:5: For his anger endureth but a moment; in his favour is life: weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning.
sourceTexts.Psalm 31:15: My times are in thy hand: deliver me from the hand of mine enemies, and from them that persecute me.
sourceTexts.Psalm 31:24: Be of good courage, and he shall strengthen your heart.
sourceTexts.Psalm 31:3: For thou art my rock and my fortress; therefore for thy name's sake lead me, and guide me.
sourceTexts.Psalm 31:9: Have mercy upon me, O LORD, for I am in trouble: mine eye is consumed with grief, yea, my soul and my belly.
sourceTexts.Psalm 32:5: I acknowledged my sin unto thee, and mine iniquity have I not hid. I said, I will confess my transgressions unto the LORD; and thou forgavest the iniquity of my sin. Selah.
sourceTexts.Psalm 32:7: Thou art my hiding place; thou shalt preserve me from trouble; thou shalt compass me about with songs of deliverance.
sourceTexts.Psalm 32:8: Now unto him that is able to do exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that worketh in us.
sourceTexts.Psalm 33:1: Rejoice in the LORD, O ye righteous: for praise is comely for the upright.
sourceTexts.Psalm 33:12: Blessed is the nation whose God is the LORD; and the people whom he hath chosen for his own inheritance.
sourceTexts.Psalm 33:16-17: There is no king saved by the multitude of an host: a mighty man is not delivered by much strength. An horse is a vain thing for safety: neither shall he deliver any by his great strength.
sourceTexts.Psalm 33:18: Behold, the eye of the Lord is upon them that fear him.
sourceTexts.Psalm 33:20-21: Our soul waiteth for the LORD: he is our help and our shield. For our heart shall rejoice in him, because we have trusted in his holy name.
sourceTexts.Psalm 33:4: The word of the Lord is right; and all his works are done in truth.
sourceTexts.Psalm 34:1: I will bless the LORD at all times: his praise shall continually be in my mouth.
sourceTexts.Psalm 34:10: The young lions do lack, and suffer hunger: but they that seek the LORD shall not want any good thing.
sourceTexts.Psalm 34:11: Come, ye children, hearken unto me: I will teach you the fear of the LORD.
sourceTexts.Psalm 34:14: Depart from evil, and do good; seek peace, and pursue it.
sourceTexts.Psalm 34:17: The righteous cry, and the Lord heareth, and delivereth them out of all their troubles.
sourceTexts.Psalm 34:18: The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.
sourceTexts.Psalm 34:19: Many are the afflictions of the righteous: but the Lord delivereth him out of them all.
sourceTexts.Psalm 34:4: I sought the Lord, and he heard me, and delivered me from all my fears.
sourceTexts.Psalm 34:5: They looked unto him, and were lightened: and their faces were not ashamed.
sourceTexts.Psalm 34:7: The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.
sourceTexts.Psalm 34:8: O taste and see that the LORD is good: blessed is the man that trusteth in him.
sourceTexts.Psalm 34:9: O fear the Lord, ye his saints: for there is no want to them that fear him.
sourceTexts.Psalm 35:9: And my soul shall be joyful in the Lord.
sourceTexts.Psalm 36:5: Thy mercy, O Lord, is in the heavens.
sourceTexts.Psalm 36:7: How excellent is thy lovingkindness, O God! therefore the children of men put their trust under the shadow of thy wings.
sourceTexts.Psalm 37:1: Fret not thyself because of evildoers, neither be thou envious against the workers of iniquity.
sourceTexts.Psalm 37:16: A little that a righteous man hath is better than the riches of many wicked.
sourceTexts.Psalm 37:23: The steps of a good man are ordered by the LORD: and he delighteth in his way.
sourceTexts.Psalm 37:25: I have been young, and now am old; yet have I not seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging bread.
sourceTexts.Psalm 37:3: Trust in the Lord, and do good; so shalt thou dwell in the land.
sourceTexts.Psalm 37:3-5: Trust in the LORD, and do good; so shalt thou dwell in the land, and verily thou shalt be fed. Delight thyself also in the LORD; and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart. Commit thy way unto the LORD; trust also in him; and he shall bring it to pass.
sourceTexts.Psalm 37:34: Wait on the LORD, and keep his way, and he shall exalt thee to inherit the land: when the wicked are cut off, thou shalt see it.
sourceTexts.Psalm 37:37: Mark the perfect man, and behold the upright: for the end of that man is peace.
sourceTexts.Psalm 37:39: But the salvation of the righteous is of the Lord: he is their strength in the time of trouble.
sourceTexts.Psalm 37:4: Delight thyself also in the Lord; and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart.
sourceTexts.Psalm 37:5: Commit thy way unto the LORD; trust also in him; and he shall bring it to pass.
sourceTexts.Psalm 37:6: And he shall bring forth thy righteousness as the light, and thy judgment as the noonday.
sourceTexts.Psalm 37:7: Rest in the LORD, and wait patiently for him: fret not thyself because of him who prospereth in his way, because of the man who bringeth wicked devices to pass.
sourceTexts.Psalm 37:8: Cease from anger, and forsake wrath: fret not thyself in any wise to do evil.
sourceTexts.Psalm 38:4: For mine iniquities are gone over mine head: as an heavy burden they are too heavy for me.
sourceTexts.Psalm 38:9: Lord, all my desire is before thee; and my groaning is not hid from thee.
sourceTexts.Psalm 40:1: I waited patiently for the Lord; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry.
sourceTexts.Psalm 40:1-2: I waited patiently for the Lord; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry. He brought me up also out of an horrible pit.
sourceTexts.Psalm 40:2: He brought me up also out of an horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set my feet upon a rock, and established my goings.
sourceTexts.Psalm 40:3: And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God: many shall see it, and fear, and shall trust in the LORD.
sourceTexts.Psalm 40:4: Blessed is that man that maketh the Lord his trust.
sourceTexts.Psalm 41:1: Blessed is he that considereth the poor: the Lord will deliver him in time of trouble.
sourceTexts.Psalm 42:1: As the hart panteth after the water brooks, so panteth my soul after thee, O God.
sourceTexts.Psalm 42:1-2: As the hart panteth after the water brooks, so panteth my soul after thee, O God. My soul thirsteth for God, for the living God: when shall I come and appear before God?
sourceTexts.Psalm 42:11: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted within me? hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him, who is the health of my countenance, and my God.
sourceTexts.Psalm 42:5: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted in me? hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him, who is the health of my countenance, and my God.
sourceTexts.Psalm 42:7: Deep calleth unto deep at the noise of thy waterspouts: all thy waves and thy billows are gone over me.
sourceTexts.Psalm 43:3: O send out thy light and thy truth: let them lead me.
sourceTexts.Psalm 43:4: Then will I go unto the altar of God, unto God my exceeding joy.
sourceTexts.Psalm 44:8: In God we boast all the day long, and praise thy name for ever.
sourceTexts.Psalm 46:1: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
sourceTexts.Psalm 46:10: Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the heathen, I will be exalted in the earth.
sourceTexts.Psalm 46:2: Therefore will not we fear, though the earth be removed, and though the mountains be carried into the midst of the sea;
sourceTexts.Psalm 46:5: God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved: God shall help her, and that right early.
sourceTexts.Psalm 46:7: The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge.
sourceTexts.Psalm 47:1: O clap your hands, all ye people; shout unto God with the voice of triumph.
sourceTexts.Psalm 48:14: For this God is our God for ever and ever: he will be our guide even unto death.
sourceTexts.Psalm 4:4: Stand in awe, and sin not: commune with your own heart upon your bed, and be still. Selah.
sourceTexts.Psalm 4:7: Thou hast put gladness in my heart, more than in the time that their corn and their wine increased.
sourceTexts.Psalm 4:8: I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety.
sourceTexts.Psalm 50:15: Call upon me in the day of trouble: I will deliver thee.
sourceTexts.Psalm 50:23: Whoso offereth praise glorifieth me: and to him that ordereth his conversation aright will I shew the salvation of God.
sourceTexts.Psalm 51:1: Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness: according unto the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions.
sourceTexts.Psalm 51:10: Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.
sourceTexts.Psalm 51:12: Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; and uphold me with thy free spirit.
sourceTexts.Psalm 51:17: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.
sourceTexts.Psalm 52:8: I am like a green olive tree in the house of God: I trust in the mercy of God for ever and ever.
sourceTexts.Psalm 54:4: Behold, God is mine helper: the Lord is with them that uphold my soul.
sourceTexts.Psalm 55:12: For it was not an enemy that reproached me; then I could have borne it: neither was it he that hated me that did magnify himself against me; then I would have hid myself from him:
sourceTexts.Psalm 55:13: But it was thou, a man mine equal, my guide, and mine acquaintance.
sourceTexts.Psalm 55:16: As for me, I will call upon God; and the Lord shall save me.
sourceTexts.Psalm 55:17: Evening, and morning, and at noon, will I pray, and cry aloud: and he shall hear my voice.
sourceTexts.Psalm 55:22: Cast thy burden upon the LORD, and he shall sustain thee: he shall never suffer the righteous to be moved.
sourceTexts.Psalm 56:3: What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee.
sourceTexts.Psalm 56:4: In God I will praise his word, in God I have put my trust; I will not fear what flesh can do unto me.
sourceTexts.Psalm 56:8: Thou tellest my wanderings: put thou my tears into thy bottle: are they not in thy book?
sourceTexts.Psalm 57:2: I will cry unto God most high; unto God that performeth all things for me.
sourceTexts.Psalm 57:7: My heart is fixed, O God, my heart is fixed: I will sing and give praise.
sourceTexts.Psalm 59:16: I will sing of thy power; yea, I will sing aloud of thy mercy.
sourceTexts.Psalm 59:17: Unto thee, O my strength, will I sing: for God is my defence.
sourceTexts.Psalm 59:9: Because of his strength will I wait upon thee: for God is my defence.
sourceTexts.Psalm 5:3: My voice shalt thou hear in the morning, O Lord.
sourceTexts.Psalm 61:2: From the end of the earth will I cry unto thee, when my heart is overwhelmed: lead me to the rock that is higher than I.
sourceTexts.Psalm 61:3: For thou hast been a shelter for me, and a strong tower from the enemy.
sourceTexts.Psalm 62:1: Truly my soul waiteth upon God: from him cometh my salvation.
sourceTexts.Psalm 62:5: My soul, wait thou only upon God; for my expectation is from him.
sourceTexts.Psalm 62:6: He only is my rock and my salvation: he is my defence.
sourceTexts.Psalm 62:8: Trust in him at all times; ye people, pour out your heart before him: God is a refuge for us. Selah.
sourceTexts.Psalm 63:1: O God, thou art my God; early will I seek thee.
sourceTexts.Psalm 63:3: Because thy lovingkindness is better than life, my lips shall praise thee.
sourceTexts.Psalm 63:5: My soul shall be satisfied as with marrow and fatness; and my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips.
sourceTexts.Psalm 64:10: The righteous shall be glad in the Lord, and shall trust in him.
sourceTexts.Psalm 65:3: Iniquities prevail against me: as for our transgressions, thou shalt purge them away.
sourceTexts.Psalm 65:4: Blessed is the man whom thou choosest, and causest to approach unto thee.
sourceTexts.Psalm 66:20: Blessed be God, which hath not turned away my prayer.
sourceTexts.Psalm 66:8: O bless our God, ye people, and make the voice of his praise to be heard.
sourceTexts.Psalm 67:1: God be merciful unto us, and bless us; and cause his face to shine upon us.
sourceTexts.Psalm 67:2: That thy way may be known upon earth, thy saving health among all nations.
sourceTexts.Psalm 67:5-7: Let the people praise thee, O God; let all the people praise thee. Then shall the earth yield her increase; and God, even our own God, shall bless us. God shall bless us; and all the ends of the earth shall fear him.
sourceTexts.Psalm 68:19: Blessed be the Lord, who daily loadeth us with benefits.
sourceTexts.Psalm 68:5: A father of the fatherless, and a judge of the widows, is God in his holy habitation.
sourceTexts.Psalm 68:6: God setteth the solitary in families: he bringeth out those which are bound with chains: but the rebellious dwell in a dry land.
sourceTexts.Psalm 69:32: The humble shall see this, and be glad: and your heart shall live that seek God.
sourceTexts.Psalm 6:9: The Lord hath heard my supplication; the Lord will receive my prayer.
sourceTexts.Psalm 70:4: Let all those that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee.
sourceTexts.Psalm 71:14: I will hope continually, and will yet praise thee more and more.
sourceTexts.Psalm 71:18: Now also when I am old and greyheaded, O God, forsake me not; until I have shewed thy strength unto this generation, and thy power to every one that is to come.
sourceTexts.Psalm 71:5: For thou art my hope, O Lord God: thou art my trust from my youth.
sourceTexts.Psalm 71:8: Let my mouth be filled with thy praise and with thy honour all the day.
sourceTexts.Psalm 71:9: Cast me not off in the time of old age; forsake me not when my strength faileth.
sourceTexts.Psalm 72:18: Blessed be the Lord God, the God of Israel, who only doeth wondrous things.
sourceTexts.Psalm 73:17: Until I went into the sanctuary of God; then understood I their end.
sourceTexts.Psalm 73:21: Thus my heart was grieved, and I was pricked in my reins.
sourceTexts.Psalm 73:25: Whom have I in heaven but thee? and there is none upon earth that I desire beside thee.
sourceTexts.Psalm 73:26: My flesh and my heart faileth: but God is the strength of my heart, and my portion for ever.
sourceTexts.Psalm 73:28: But it is good for me to draw near to God: I have put my trust in the Lord GOD, that I may declare all thy works.
sourceTexts.Psalm 74:12: For God is my King of old, working salvation in the midst of the earth.
sourceTexts.Psalm 75:1: Unto thee, O God, do we give thanks, unto thee do we give thanks.
sourceTexts.Psalm 76:4: Thou art more glorious and excellent than the mountains of prey.
sourceTexts.Psalm 77:10: And I said, This is my infirmity: but I will remember the years of the right hand of the most High.
sourceTexts.Psalm 77:14: Thou art the God that doest wonders: thou hast declared thy strength among the people.
sourceTexts.Psalm 78:4: We will not hide them from their children, shewing to the generation to come the praises of the Lord.
sourceTexts.Psalm 79:13: So we thy people and sheep of thy pasture will give thee thanks for ever.
sourceTexts.Psalm 7:10: My defence is of God, which saveth the upright in heart.
sourceTexts.Psalm 80:3: Turn us again, O God, and cause thy face to shine; and we shall be saved.
sourceTexts.Psalm 81:10: I am the Lord thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt: open thy mouth wide, and I will fill it.
sourceTexts.Psalm 82:3: Defend the poor and fatherless: do justice to the afflicted and needy.
sourceTexts.Psalm 84:10: For a day in thy courts is better than a thousand. I had rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God, than to dwell in the tents of wickedness.
sourceTexts.Psalm 84:11: For the Lord God is a sun and shield: the Lord will give grace and glory.
sourceTexts.Psalm 84:12: O Lord of hosts, blessed is the man that trusteth in thee.
sourceTexts.Psalm 84:3: Yea, the sparrow hath found an house, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she may lay her young, even thine altars, O LORD of hosts, my King, and my God.
sourceTexts.Psalm 84:5: Blessed is the man whose strength is in thee; in whose heart are the ways of them.
sourceTexts.Psalm 85:6: Wilt thou not revive us again: that thy people may rejoice in thee?
sourceTexts.Psalm 86:11: Teach me thy way, O LORD; I will walk in thy truth: unite my heart to fear thy name.
sourceTexts.Psalm 86:15: But thou, O Lord, art a God full of compassion, and gracious, longsuffering, and plenteous in mercy and truth.
sourceTexts.Psalm 86:5: For thou, Lord, art good, and ready to forgive.
sourceTexts.Psalm 86:6: Give ear, O LORD, unto my prayer; and attend to the voice of my supplications.
sourceTexts.Psalm 87:3: Glorious things are spoken of thee, O city of God.
sourceTexts.Psalm 88:1: O LORD God of my salvation, I have cried day and night before thee:
sourceTexts.Psalm 88:13: But unto thee have I cried, O Lord; and in the morning shall my prayer prevent thee.
sourceTexts.Psalm 89:1: I will sing of the mercies of the Lord for ever.
sourceTexts.Psalm 89:15: Blessed is the people that know the joyful sound: they shall walk, O Lord, in the light of thy countenance.
sourceTexts.Psalm 8:2: Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings hast thou ordained strength.
sourceTexts.Psalm 8:3: When I consider thy heavens, the work of thy fingers, the moon and the stars, which thou hast ordained;
sourceTexts.Psalm 90:12: So teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom.
sourceTexts.Psalm 90:14: O satisfy us early with thy mercy; that we may rejoice and be glad all our days.
sourceTexts.Psalm 90:17: And let the beauty of the Lord our God be upon us: and establish thou the work of our hands upon us; yea, the work of our hands establish thou it.
sourceTexts.Psalm 90:2: Before the mountains were brought forth, or ever thou hadst formed the earth and the world, even from everlasting to everlasting, thou art God.
sourceTexts.Psalm 91:1: He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.
sourceTexts.Psalm 91:1-2: He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty. I will say of the Lord, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust.
sourceTexts.Psalm 91:11: For he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways.
sourceTexts.Psalm 91:14: Because he hath set his love upon me, therefore will I deliver him: I will set him on high, because he hath known my name.
sourceTexts.Psalm 91:15: He shall call upon me, and I will answer him: I will be with him in trouble; I will deliver him, and honour him.
sourceTexts.Psalm 91:16: With long life will I satisfy him, and shew him my salvation.
sourceTexts.Psalm 91:2: I will say of the LORD, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust.
sourceTexts.Psalm 91:4: He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust: his truth shall be thy shield and buckler.
sourceTexts.Psalm 92:1: It is a good thing to give thanks unto the LORD, and to sing praises unto thy name, O most High:
sourceTexts.Psalm 92:1-4: It is a good thing to give thanks unto the LORD, and to sing praises unto thy name, O most High: To shew forth thy lovingkindness in the morning, and thy faithfulness every night, Upon an instrument of ten strings, and upon the psaltery; upon the harp with a solemn sound. For thou, LORD, hast made me glad through thy work: I will triumph in the works of thy hands.
sourceTexts.Psalm 92:14: They shall still bring forth fruit in old age; they shall be fat and flourishing;
sourceTexts.Psalm 92:4: For thou, Lord, hast made me glad through thy work.
sourceTexts.Psalm 93:4: The Lord on high is mightier than the noise of many waters.
sourceTexts.Psalm 94:18: When I said, My foot slippeth; thy mercy, O Lord, held me up.
sourceTexts.Psalm 94:19: In the multitude of my thoughts within me thy comforts delight my soul.
sourceTexts.Psalm 94:22: But the LORD is my defence; and my God is the rock of my refuge.
sourceTexts.Psalm 95:1: O come, let us sing unto the Lord: let us make a joyful noise to the rock of our salvation.
sourceTexts.Psalm 95:1-2: O come, let us sing unto the LORD: let us make a joyful noise to the rock of our salvation. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving, and make a joyful noise unto him with psalms.
sourceTexts.Psalm 95:1-7: O come, let us sing unto the LORD: let us make a joyful noise to the rock of our salvation. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving, and make a joyful noise unto him with psalms. For the LORD is a great God, and a great King above all gods. In his hand are the deep places of the earth: the strength of the hills is his also. The sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. O come, let us worship and bow down: let us kneel before the LORD our maker. For he is our God; and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand. To day if ye will hear his voice,
sourceTexts.Psalm 95:2: Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving, and make a joyful noise unto him with psalms.
sourceTexts.Psalm 95:6: O come, let us worship and bow down: let us kneel before the LORD our maker.
sourceTexts.Psalm 95:7: For he is our God; and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand.
sourceTexts.Psalm 96:1: O sing unto the Lord a new song: sing unto the Lord, all the earth.
sourceTexts.Psalm 96:2: Sing unto the Lord, bless his name; shew forth his salvation from day to day.
sourceTexts.Psalm 97:11: Light is sown for the righteous, and gladness for the upright in heart.
sourceTexts.Psalm 98:1: O sing unto the LORD a new song; for he hath done marvellous things: his right hand, and his holy arm, hath gotten him the victory.
sourceTexts.Psalm 99:2: The Lord is great in Zion; and he is high above all the people.
sourceTexts.Psalm 9:1: I will praise thee, O LORD, with my whole heart; I will shew forth all thy marvellous works.
sourceTexts.Psalm 9:9: The LORD also will be a refuge for the oppressed, a refuge in times of trouble.
sourceTexts.Romans 10:14-15: How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!
sourceTexts.Romans 10:9-10: That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved. For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.
sourceTexts.Romans 12:6-8: Having then gifts differing according to the grace that is given unto us, whether prophecy, let us prophesy according to the proportion of faith; Or ministry, let us wait on our ministering: or he that teacheth, on teaching; Or he that exhorteth, on exhortation: he that giveth, let him do it with simplicity; he that ruleth, with diligence; he that sheweth mercy, with cheerfulness.
sourceTexts.Romans 1:16-17: For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.
sourceTexts.Romans 4:20-21: He staggered not at the promise of God through unbelief; but was strong in faith, giving glory to God; And being fully persuaded that, what he had promised, he was able also to perform.
sourceTexts.Romans 5:3-4: And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope:
sourceTexts.Romans 8:16-17: The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.
sourceTexts.Romans 8:26-27: Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered. And he that searcheth the hearts knoweth what is the mind of the Spirit, because he maketh intercession for the saints according to the will of God.
sourceTexts.Romans 8:38-39: For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
sourceTexts.Titus 2:11-12: For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men, Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world.
sourceTexts.Titus 3:5-6: Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost; Which he shed on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Saviour;
